heading: INT. FORMER MATTRESS SHOWROOM - ESCAPE ROOM "THE SLEEPLESS VAULT" - DAY

units.text: INT. FORMER MATTRESS SHOWROOM - ESCAPE ROOM "THE SLEEPLESS VAULT" - DAY
A warehouse of bare walls painted dark purple.
A countdown clock glows on a screen: 60:00.
Dozens of mattress boxes sit stacked to the ceiling, and a single door has a combination lock on it.
GRANT PELLEGRINO, forties, regional manager in a quarter-zip, stands in the center of the room with his arms crossed.
WANJIRU KAMAU, thirties, his analyst, sits on a mattress crate holding the instruction card.
FRANCINE DUBOIS, fifties, accounts payable, leans against the wall in orthopedic shoes.
He claps his hands once, a sound like a pistol.
She does not look up.
The other woman does, slowly.
Okay, team! The clock is ticking!
units.name: GRANT

units.text: It's an hour.
units.name: WANJIRU

units.text: And we'll need every minute of it.
units.name: GRANT

units.text: He strides to the lock, tries four numbers, and grunts when it doesn't open.
She flips the card over.
It says only: "THE CODE IS WHERE YOU SLEEP."
That's a bed.
units.name: FRANCINE

units.text: Francine, don't be literal.
units.name: GRANT

units.text: It's a literal room.
units.name: FRANCINE

units.text: He rips a lid off a mattress box.
Inside: nothing.
He tears off another.
Then another.
Foam peanuts spill across the floor like snow.
She watches him with the patience of someone who has been through budget season.
Grant, maybe we should read the clues first.
units.name: WANJIRU

units.text: I'm reading them with my hands.
units.name: GRANT

units.text: The clock hits 52:00.
Wanjiru stands, crosses to the wall, and runs her fingers along a row of numbered pillows.
One to nine. Someone's arranged these.
units.name: WANJIRU

units.text: Count them again.
units.name: FRANCINE

units.text: She does.
Her lips move.
She stops at six, frowns, lifts pillow six and finds a brass key taped underneath.
She holds it up.
Grant lunges.
She steps back and his hand closes on air.
Give me that.
units.name: GRANT

units.text: It's a team game, Grant.
units.name: WANJIRU

units.text: I'm the team lead.
units.name: GRANT

units.text: Then lead.
units.name: FRANCINE

units.text: Nobody speaks.
The clock ticks.
Grant lowers his hand and looks at the floor, at the peanuts clinging to his shoes.
Then at the key, shining in Wanjiru's palm.
He drags a hand down his face.
Fine. Fine. What do you want to do?
units.name: GRANT

units.text: Wanjiru offers the key to Francine, who studies it, turns it over, and tucks it into the pocket of her cardigan.
First, we eat lunch.
units.name: FRANCINE

units.text: Lunch? The clock
units.name: GRANT

units.text: It's twelve-fifteen. I've missed lunch every Thursday for nine years.
units.name: FRANCINE

units.text: She takes a Tupperware out of her purse, sits on a mattress, and opens it.
The smell of curry fills the room.
Wanjiru grins and sits beside her.
Grant stares, then slowly lowers himself to a crate.
She hands him a plastic fork.
The clock drops to 49:00.
For a long minute nobody does anything but chew.
Then Grant begins to laugh, short, helpless bursts, until he's wiping his eyes with the quarter-zip.
She laughs too, quietly, and so does Francine.
I've been so tired.
units.name: GRANT

units.text: We know.
units.name: WANJIRU

units.text: He pulls off his lanyard and lets it fall onto the mattress.
Then he picks it back up, folds it, and puts it in his pocket.
Francine hands him a second fork.
He takes a bite.
This is really good.
units.name: GRANT

units.text: It's my mother's.
units.name: FRANCINE

units.text: The clock goes on counting down above their heads, and none of them looks at it.
